summary: The simulation runs end-to-end and produces basic metrics, but key issues reduce fidelity and hinder evaluation. The most critical problems are: (1) evaluation is not aligned with the prediction window (days 30–39); (2) early convergence stopping can truncate the forecast period; (3) behavioral validation metrics (Rb, churn) are not compared against observed data even though train_data.csv contains microstates; and (4) new adopters are counted via first_adoption_day, which misses re-adoptions after dropouts. Addressing these will substantially improve correctness, interpretability, and alignment with the task specification.

critical_issues.issue: Evaluation window mismatch with task (predictions should be evaluated over days 30–39, but RMSE is computed over whatever overlap exists with train_data.csv)
critical_issues.impact: Misleading accuracy assessment; RMSE of ~0.31 likely reflects in-sample training window (days 0–29) rather than the holdout forecast window (days 30–39).
critical_issues.solution: Store observed adoption by explicit day index; evaluate RMSE/TimeTo50 strictly within [prediction_start_day, prediction_end_day] when observed data exists; otherwise skip or report that holdout observations are missing. Also export the forecast series for days 30–39.

critical_issues.issue: Early termination before completing the prediction window due to convergence check
critical_issues.impact: Forecast horizon may be cut short, producing incomplete or biased forecasts for days 30–39.
critical_issues.solution: Gate convergence termination so it cannot trigger before the prediction_end_day has been simulated.

critical_issues.issue: Behavioral validation metrics Rb and churn are NaN because observed counterparts are not computed from microdata
critical_issues.impact: Lack of validation on contagion strength and retention dynamics; reduces confidence in model mechanisms.
critical_issues.solution: Compute observed Rb and churn directly from train_data.csv by differencing per-agent wearing_mask between consecutive days; then compare with simulated series over the overlapping window.

critical_issues.issue: New adopters are counted via first_adoption_day only
critical_issues.impact: Re-adoptions after dropouts are not counted as new adoptions; Rb and churn metrics are distorted.
critical_issues.solution: Return and aggregate adopted_today events from the adoption module (including scheduled activations and immediate adoptions) rather than relying on first_adoption_day.

critical_issues.issue: Observed series stored as an unlabeled list loses explicit day indices
critical_issues.impact: Fragile alignment between observed and simulated days; breaks if the observed days do not start at 0 or are not contiguous.
critical_issues.solution: Store observed adoption as a dict day->rate to align precisely by day; use these day keys for evaluation.

model_improvements.current_approach: Evaluate RMSE over the overlapping length of observed and simulated series without enforcing [30–39].
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Respect MODEL_PLAN prediction_start_day and prediction_end_day; compute RMSE and timing error within this window only if observed data for those days exist; else notify and just export predictions.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Correct evaluation against the task’s forecast window; avoids leakage from training period.

model_improvements.current_approach: Terminate when adoption rate stabilizes even if the forecast window is not reached.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Disable convergence-based early stopping until after prediction_end_day.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Ensures full prediction horizon is simulated; avoids truncated outputs.

model_improvements.suggested_approach: Compute observed Rb and churn from train_data.csv using per-agent day-to-day transitions; compare to simulated series with MAE over overlapping days.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Improved mechanistic validation and calibration of complex contagion and retention dynamics.

model_improvements.current_approach: Use first_adoption_day to count new adopters, missing re-adoptions.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Track adopted_today events and pass them to the aggregator for accurate new adopter counts.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: More accurate Rb and churn metrics; better reflection of dynamics with drop/re-adopt.

model_improvements.current_approach: Only difference across groups; gini_coefficient unused.
model_improvements.suggested_approach: Compute both difference and Gini for group inequality; report both for richer diagnostics.
model_improvements.expected_benefit: Better understanding of heterogeneity in adoption by group.

code_improvements.modification: Store observed adoption as day->rate dict; evaluate only over [prediction_start_day, prediction_end_day]; compute observed Rb/churn from train_data and compare to simulated series.
code_improvements.reason: Aligns evaluation with the forecast window and adds key behavioral validation metrics.

code_improvements.modification: Gate convergence-based early termination so it cannot fire before prediction_end_day is simulated.
code_improvements.reason: Prevents premature termination that would truncate the forecast period.

code_improvements.modification: Return adopted_today events from the adoption module and pass them to the aggregator; count new adopters from events rather than first_adoption_day.
code_improvements.reason: Correctly counts re-adoptions and supports accurate Rb/churn computation.

code_improvements.modification: Also export a filtered CSV for predictions in days 30–39 (or configured window).
code_improvements.reason: Provides direct artifact for the prediction period and downstream scoring.

code_improvements.modification: Add Gini inequality alongside difference; include policy_effect_size in results for diagnostics.
code_improvements.reason: Richer diagnostics to calibrate subgroup and policy effects.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: RMSE computed over training days rather than forecast window.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Evaluate strictly on [prediction_start_day, prediction_end_day]; if no observed data available for that window, clearly indicate and focus on exporting predictions.
Compute observed Rb from train_data by differencing per-agent mask states; calibrate b1/b2 (neighbors and quadratic terms) to match early Rb.
Compute observed dropouts via (mask_t=0 & mask_{t-1}=1); calibrate drop_logit_intercept and betas to match observed churn levels.

data_alignment_suggestions.current_gap: Computed internally but not reported for validation.
data_alignment_suggestions.suggestion: Export policy_effect_size and compare pre/post slopes around Day 10 to observed trend change in train_data.

prioritized_actions: Align evaluation with the prediction window (days 30–39) and gate early termination until after day 39.
Compute observed Rb and churn from train_data and compare to simulated series (MAE).
Track adopted_today events and use them for Rb and churn computation; stop relying on first_adoption_day for event counts.
Export a separate predictions CSV for the forecast window; include adoption_rate and Rb/churn slices.
Add Gini inequality and policy_effect_size to results for diagnostics; calibrate parameters to reduce RMSE and timing error.
additional_comments: Overall design and modularization are solid. The multiplex network, policy/messaging, and logistic adoption with quadratic terms provide a good base. Most remaining work is in evaluation alignment, event counting, and adding observed behavioral metrics for Rb and churn to calibrate model dynamics. Keep the main() call at the end for sandbox compatibility.

change_analysis.summary: No recent code changes were recorded in the diff. The current issues stem from initial implementation choices around evaluation scope, event counting, and validation metrics.
positive_impacts: Stable end-to-end execution with multiplex network, policy/messaging, and adoption/dropout modules.
Reasonable modular structure enabling targeted improvements.
negative_impacts: Evaluation not aligned with forecast window; can misrepresent performance.
NaN for key behavioral validation metrics (Rb, churn).
New adopters counted via first_adoption_day, missing re-adoptions.
suggestions: Anchor evaluation to the prediction window explicitly and export forecast artifacts.
Leverage train_data microstates to compute observed Rb and churn for better calibration.
Adopt event-based counting (adopted_today) to drive Rb and churn metrics.
